What Notched Sound does: First, you find the exact pitch of the ringing in each ear. The app then takes soothing background sounds (like rain or ocean waves) or your own music and quietly carves out a ‘silent window’—a notch—right where your ringing sits, while keeping the rest of the sound full and natural.

How it helps tinnitus: Tinnitus happens when the hearing cells in your brain tuned to a specific pitch stay switched on and overactive. By removing that exact pitch from what you listen to while gently playing the healthy sounds around it, your brain’s neighbouring hearing cells naturally calm the overactive ones down. Listening with headphones for 1 to 2 hours a day helps train your brain to turn down the volume of the ringing over time.
1. Match the Ringing in Each Ear (Wear Headphones)
Put on headphones and match the sound and loudness of the ringing in your left and right ears separately. You can also whistle or hum the sound into your microphone. During fine-tuning, tap the ½× / 2× buttons to test half or double the pitch—it is very easy to mistake a higher or lower twin note for your actual ringing.
2. Choose Your Notch Size & Comfortable Volume
Tap the sliders icon at the top right to choose how wide the silent gap is and set your volume. Pick 1 oct (a wider gap—best if your ringing wavers or feels spread out) or 0.5 oct (a narrower gap—best for a single, steady whistle), where an ‘octave’ simply means the span from one musical note to its higher twin. You can also tap Compare Filter to briefly switch the notch off and hear the difference. Keep the volume comfortable so the solid volume line on the graph sits at or just below the dotted ringing line.
3. Listen to Soothing Sounds or Your Own Music
Relax with gentle background sounds like rainfall, ocean surf, or soft noise on the Soundscapes tab, or choose a folder of your own songs on the Music tab—the app automatically filters out your ringing pitch as you listen.
4. Set a Sleep Timer & Keep Playback Running
Use Session Duration to set how long you want to listen, and tick the 5-minute sleep fade-out if you are winding down for bed. Finally, allow the app to run unrestricted in Battery Optimisation so your phone doesn’t pause the sound when your screen turns off.
